result.summary: This signalized intersection features a wide roadway with embedded trolley tracks but lacks visible marked crosswalks or dedicated pedestrian signals. While sidewalks are present, the high number of travel lanes and lack of designated crossing infrastructure create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: No painted markings define a safe path for pedestrians across the wide intersection, despite the presence of traffic signals.

hazards.name: Embedded trolley tracks
hazards.description: Tracks in the roadway create tripping hazards for pedestrians and can catch bicycle tires.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to spend a significant amount of time exposed to traffic without a refuge island.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment is a residential intersection adjacent to high-density housing, characterized by a lack of formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, the absence of marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals increases risk for residents in this high-density area.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks at this intersection despite the presence of a large apartment building, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated space.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and the large vehicle in the foreground obscure the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and along the curb line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian countdown signals to the existing traffic light infrastructure.

result.summary: The environment features a wide roadway with integrated trolley tracks and a marked zebra crosswalk. While sidewalks and basic traffic signals are present, the lack of pedestrian-specific signals and the long crossing distance increase exposure risk.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Tracks in the roadway can be a trip hazard or catch bicycle wheels.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible at this signalized intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center to allow two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated signals to provide clear crossing information.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and sidewalks. However, the presence of embedded tracks in the foreground and large trees at the corners introduces potential trip hazards and sightline obstructions for road users.

hazards.name: Embedded tracks
hazards.description: Tracks embedded in the roadway surface can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch bicycle wheels.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground across the bottom of the frame

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from vegetation
hazards.description: Large, low-hanging trees may block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Upper center and right side of the intersection

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven surfaces near the tracks create a trip hazard.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and level the pavement around the embedded tracks to eliminate trip hazards.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim low-hanging branches to ensure clear sightlines at the intersection corners.
